clue.text: Boorish northern smoker meets author

parts.note: lum is a Scottish and northern English word for a chimney, something that smokes
to pen a book is to author it

explanation.surface: A rough northern pipe-smoker gets together with a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smoker' is not a person but a chimney; LUM is the Scots word for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumpen describes the coarse, uncultured masses, so it is a synonym for boorish in a dismissive sense.

clue.text: Impractical UN holding up seaworthy vessel

indicators.note: the letters of UN hold the next part between them, one at each end
in a down clue, up means the piece is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: A1 at Lloyd's describes a ship in first-class condition; A1 written as AI
a pot is a vessel for holding things

explanation.surface: The United Nations is accused of being unrealistic for delaying a ship fit to sail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses AIPOT to give TOPIA, which sits between U and N. A1 is the Lloyd's Register grade for a fully seaworthy ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopian schemes are idealistic and unworkable, so the word is a synonym for impractical.

clue.text: Secretary travelling again to arid tableland

parts.note: PA is personal assistant, a secretary

indicators.note: travelling suggests the letters moving about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A secretary sets off once more on a trip to a dry plateau.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges AGAIN TO into TAGONIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Patagonia in southern Argentina is largely dry steppe plateau, a specific example of an arid tableland.

clue.text: Wanderer bathes old woman in green light

indicators.note: to bathe something is to surround it with liquid, so the outer piece encloses the inner

parts.note: a nod is a go-ahead, the green light for a plan
ma is an informal word for mother, one's old woman

explanation.surface: A traveller washes an elderly lady under a green glow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green light' is not a colour but approval given with a nod of the head; 'bathes' wraps it round the old woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad has no fixed home and roams from place to place, so is a wanderer.

clue.text: Knight detaining old silly demands gold coin

indicators.note: detaining means holding something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to dub someone is to make them a knight with a tap of the sword
a loon is a silly person, as in 'you silly'

explanation.surface: A knight holds back a foolish old man who insists on payment in gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knight' is a verb here, the act of knighting, and 'detaining' puts the old letter inside it; 'demands' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A doubloon was a Spanish gold piece, the classic pirate treasure.

clue.text: Drive home skirting large oval mound

indicators.note: skirting means going round the edge, so the outer letters wrap the inner

parts.note: to drum in a point is to drive it home by repetition
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A driver heads home avoiding a big egg-shaped hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive home' is the phrasal verb for hammering a point, and 'skirting' sets the size letter between its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A drumlin is an elongated, egg-shaped hill of glacial debris, a precise geological sense of oval mound.

clue.text: Single male penetrates novel in Dutch

indicators.note: to penetrate is to get inside, so this piece goes into the other
novel means new, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: An unmarried man breaks into a book written in Dutch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges IN DUTCH to UNITCHD, and HE goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To get hitched is to marry, so someone unhitched is not married: single.

clue.text: Shakespearean king with new master

parts.note: King Lear is the title character of Shakespeare's tragedy

explanation.surface: An old king from the plays accompanies a young teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: To master a skill is to learn it thoroughly; the verb senses are synonyms.

clue.text: Manage lines in Old English

indicators.note: in places the poetry piece within the abbreviation for the old language

parts.note: verse is lines of poetry

explanation.surface: Someone copes with poetry written in Anglo-Saxon.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee a project is to supervise or run it, a synonym for manage.

clue.text: Harbour gates opening

parts.note: a port in old use is a gate or gateway, as in Latin porta
a mouth is an opening, as of a cave or bottle

explanation.surface: A dock gate standing open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harbour' looks like the start of a description of gates, but it is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Portsmouth is the great naval harbour on England's south coast, so it is an example of a harbour.

clue.text: Criminally endorse last thirteen letters?

definitions.meaning: to encourage or assist someone in wrongdoing
the second half of the word alphabet, as the last thirteen letters are the second half of the alphabet

explanation.walkthrough: The word ALPHABET splits as ALPH and ABET, so its second half playfully stands for the alphabet's second half, N to Z.
explanation.definitionFit: To aid and support a crime is the legal sense of the verb, so endorsing a wrongdoing criminally fits.

clue.text: Surrounded in Reading — molested leaving area

indicators.note: molested means interfered with, so the remaining letters are disturbed into a new order
leaving means going away from the word, so that letter is taken out

explanation.surface: A news report of someone encircled in the Berkshire town after being harassed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' removes A from READING to leave REDING, which 'molested' rearranges. Reading is a town west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ringed is circled all round, so the word is a synonym for surrounded.

clue.text: Can one enter final as classics scholar?

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so these pieces go into the other word

parts.note: last means final
a tin is a can
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A question whether a student of Greek and Latin may sit the last exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like the verb of the question but is the noun, a container; 'enter' sends it and the numeral into the word for final.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latinist is an expert in Latin, a classics scholar.

clue.text: Man one to be flayed soon

indicators.note: flaying strips off the skin, so only the letters within the phrase, without its outer ones, are kept

explanation.surface: A grim threat that a man will be skinned shortly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be flayed' removes M and E, the outside letters of MAN ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: In old or literary use the adverb means presently, in a little while: soon.

clue.text: Don perhaps changing jumper on beach

indicators.note: changing means the letters swap about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An academic, maybe, swapping a sweater by the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' suggests a sweater, a British word for a pullover; here it is a creature that jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: The sandhopper is a small crustacean that leaps about on the shore, so is a jumper found on beaches.

clue.text: Face children to reveal minor affair

parts.note: a side is a face, as of a cube
issue means offspring, children

explanation.surface: Someone confronts their offspring to own up to a small fling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affair' suggests an illicit romance but means simply a matter.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter of secondary importance, beside the main point, is a minor affair.

clue.text: Paper page merchant distributed

indicators.note: distributed means spread around, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A trader hands out a sheet of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' rearranges MERCHANT to ARCHMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Parchment is prepared animal skin used as a writing material, and also a heavy paper imitating it.

clue.text: Catherine's execution in this tale?

parts.note: Catherine Howard, fifth wife of Henry VIII, was beheaded, so her end is a ..., the title of E M Forster's novel

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads the novel's title literally, as the death of a Howard.
explanation.definitionFit: The Forster novel of 1910 is a tale whose title, read literally, describes the beheading of a Howard queen.

clue.text: Blade-wielder beheaded sailors in sultanate

indicators.note: in places the sailors inside the country's name

parts.note: Oman is a sultanate on the Arabian peninsula

indicators.note: beheaded means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: tars are sailors

explanation.surface: A sword-swinging killer decapitates seamen in an Arab state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' drops the first letter of the sailors, and 'in' puts what is left inside the Gulf sultanate.
explanation.definitionFit: Oars have blades, so a rower is cheekily someone who wields a blade.

clue.text: Ultimately servile brute an individual who succeeds

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter is taken

parts.note: a pig is a brute, a nasty person
one means an, a single one

explanation.surface: A grovelling beast eventually proves to be a winner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'succeeds' looks like triumphing but means coming after.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigone is a follower or lesser successor of a great figure, someone who succeeds in the sense of coming after.

clue.text: Republican to employ stratagem

parts.note: to use is to employ

explanation.surface: A politician resorts to a trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruse is a trick or scheme intended to deceive, so it is a synonym for stratagem.

clue.text: Warlord keeps head from thermonuclear weapon

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: a shogun was a Japanese military ruler

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A warlord retains the warhead of an H-bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps' puts T inside SHOGUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A shotgun is a smooth-bore firearm, an example of a weapon.

clue.text: One follows exotic birds in Italian port

indicators.note: follows means comes after, so this letter goes at the end
exotic means strange and foreign, so these letters take an unusual order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher tracks rare species in a harbour town in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' rearranges BIRDS IN to BRINDIS, then I is placed after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Brindisi is a seaport on the Adriatic in the heel of Italy, an example of an Italian port.

clue.text: Fool about with explosive component

parts.note: a nit is a fool, a nitwit
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: An idiot messes around with part of a bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre, potassium nitrate, is a main ingredient of gunpowder, so is a component of explosives.

clue.text: Second husband in sophisticated company

indicators.note: in places the husband's letter inside the word for sophisticated

parts.note: cool means stylish, sophisticated

explanation.surface: A woman's next husband moves in a smart crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'company' suggests a firm or group of guests; it is a group of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A school is a large group of fish or whales swimming together, a company of them.

clue.text: Bayonet in male side

definitions.meaning: to bayonet is to stab with a pointed blade, impale
the ... side of a family is its male line, the distaff side the female

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link: the second definition draws on the old phrase 'spear side' for descent through the male line.
explanation.definitionFit: Stabbing with a point is the verb sense, and the weapon names the male line in genealogy.

clue.text: Obscene material corporations rejected

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a corporation is a jocular old word for a pot belly, a tum

explanation.surface: Big companies turn down pornography.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporations' are not firms but paunches.
explanation.definitionFit: Smut is indecent writing or pictures, obscene material.

clue.text: Whole chicken gets cooked outside tourist site

indicators.note: outside means placed around the other letters
cooked means doctored or messed about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: one means whole, united
a hen is a chicken

explanation.surface: A whole bird is roasted out of doors by a holidaymaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges GETS into two pairs, ST and GE, which 'outside' places at either end of ONEHEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The prehistoric circle on Salisbury Plain draws over a million visitors a year, an example of a tourist site.

clue.text: Come before volcano in retreat and surrender

indicators.note: in retreat means going backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: Etna is the volcano on Sicily
to cede is to give up, surrender

explanation.surface: People falling back from an erupting mountain and giving up.
explanation.definitionFit: To antecede something is to precede it in time or order.

clue.text: Seaman in position

definitions.meaning: a ranking or standing, a position on a scale

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Naval non-officers are called ratings, and a grade or ranking is also one.
